clean – Transform

src/flask_website/clean.py

Clean raw GradCafe scrape output into structured applicant records.

This module is the transform stage of the ETL pipeline. It takes the raw text fields written by scrape and, using regular expressions, splits them into structured fields: program, degree, comments, date added, status, term, applicant nationality, GRE Quant/Verbal/AW and GPA.

Output field names match what load_data expects (program, comments, date_added, url, status, term, US/International, GRE, GRE V, GRE AW, GPA, Degree). Empty fields are omitted from each record (except comments).

Example:

python clean.py -i applicant_data.json -o cleaned_applicant_data_new.json

clean._extract_degree(program_text)[source]

Split the trailing degree token (Masters/PhD/…) off the program text.

Parameters:

program_text (str) – Raw program text, e.g. "Speech Language Pathology Masters".

(program_name, degree), e.g. ("Speech Language Pathology", "Masters"). degree is "" if no recognised suffix is found.

Return type:

clean._extract_comment(meta_text)[source]

Strip the structured prefix off the meta text, leaving the comment.

The prefix (status/date/term/type/GRE/GPA) is matched by _META_PREFIX_RE; whatever remains is the applicant’s free-text comment.

Parameters:

meta_text (str) – Raw metadata/comment text.

Returns:

The free-text comment, possibly "".

Return type:

str

clean.clean_data(raw_entries)[source]

Turn raw scraped entries into cleaned, structured entries.

Input entries use the keys produced by scrape._parse_page() (raw_school_text, raw_program_text, raw_comment_text, raw_added_on_text, raw_decision_text, raw_meta_text, url). Output entries are ready for the llm-generated-program / llm-generated-university tagging step and, after that, load_data.

Parameters:

raw_entries (list[dict]) – Raw scraper output.

Returns:

One cleaned dictionary per input entry, in the same order.

Return type:

list[dict]

>>> clean_data([{"raw_school_text": "MIT",
...              "raw_program_text": "Computer Science PhD",
...              "raw_meta_text": "Accepted Fall 2026 International GPA 3.90"}])[0]["Degree"]
'PhD'
